recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Future changes should only be made through a new FHIR-I decision that revisits current RESTful async or messaging behavior; this old tracker is already satisfied and superseded by later async work.
issue_request: FHIR-7944 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core issue raised against DSTU1 operations text. It proposed using callback URLs for asynchronous operation execution, but the approved resolution said to move section 2.2.0.6 to the messaging page, refer to it from the asynchronous section, and rewrite the note accordingly.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly names FHIR-7944, but the Jira comment records svn revision 5657. Git-svn commit 8b801ae887a7ed1c4e58cb57c30a8379b50cf157 is build@5657 and removed the detailed message-based asynchronous operation instructions from source/operations.html while adding operation invocation via messages to source/messaging.html, matching the modified resolution.
additional_context: FHIR-6336 is the duplicate/same-change-family issue and confirms the intent to remove the confusing operations-page async section. Later final decisions FHIR-35936, FHIR-41202, and FHIR-47271 updated the current async page around RESTful async patterns, operation synchronicity, and pattern disambiguation, so current operation async behavior should be interpreted through async.html rather than the 2015 DSTU messaging note or the originally proposed callback scheme.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. Current source/operations.html directs asynchronous operation execution to the standard RESTful API async pattern, source/async.html describes the current RFC 7240-based patterns and conformance, and source/messaging.html separately retains operation invocation via messages. Adding callback URL prose or restoring the old operations-page messaging detail would be stale and potentially misleading.
